issue.title: replace tool converts TypeScript string escape sequences into literal newlines
issue.body:
During #3781 work, the built-in `replace` tool received `new_string` containing TypeScript `.join('\n\n')` and `.split('\n')` code (backslash-n characters within single quotes). It reported successful replacements but the resulting file contained actual line breaks between the single quotes. Bun and tsc failed with `Unterminated string literal` at scripts/pr-review-walkthrough.ts:279,282,302,320. Reading the file confirmed the escaped sequences had become physical newlines.

The same code supplied through `apply_patch` preserved the backslash-n sequences. Logs: `tmp/verify3781-next/green-stages.log` and `types-initial.log` in branch-6.

Expected: replace preserves literal `old_string`/`new_string` content, including source-code escapes, as its tool contract describes. This creates invalid source from valid tool input and forces patch-based recovery.

steps: Create sample.ts with exactly this one-line TypeScript source and a final newline: const value = "old";. Read it with read_file.
expected: Exact replacement preserves literal source-code escape sequences after JSON decoding.
defect: replace writes physical newline/CR control characters where new_string contained literal backslash escape sequences, corrupting source code.
Root cause: The observed behavior is consistent with an additional escape-normalization step after JSON decoding, which makes literal backslash-n indistinguishable from an actual newline. The reports do not identify a confirmed implementation line; do not label an arbitrary edit helper as the root cause.
